name: OpenObserve
tagline: Single-binary Rust observability platform storing logs, metrics and traces as Parquet on object storage.
description: OpenObserve, originally ZincObserve from the team behind ZincSearch, is an observability platform that ingests logs, metrics, traces, real-user monitoring and session replays and stores them as Parquet files on S3-compatible storage. It queries them with SQL through Apache DataFusion, plus PromQL for metrics. It ships as one binary with built-in UI, dashboards, alerts and ingestion pipelines, positioning itself as a cheaper replacement for Elasticsearch and Kibana or for SaaS tools such as Datadog. The open-source build is AGPL-3.0; the Enterprise edition, free below a daily ingest threshold, adds SSO, RBAC and federated search, and OpenObserve Cloud is the hosted option.

license.name: GNU AGPL v3.0 (open source); Enterprise is commercial

pricing.notes: Open source is free; Enterprise is free under an ingest threshold; OpenObserve Cloud bills by ingested data.

scale.notes: Stateless ingesters and queriers over object storage; HA mode uses NATS and a metadata store.

strengths: Logs, metrics, traces, RUM and dashboards in one binary
Parquet on object storage keeps retention cost low
SQL for log analytics instead of a bespoke query language
Elasticsearch-compatible ingest lets existing shippers point at it
Simple single-node start with a path to HA clusters
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 licence, with SSO and RBAC in the commercial edition
Young project; APIs and storage formats have changed quickly
Broad scope means some features are shallower than specialised tools
Object-storage reads make cold queries slower than local indexes
useCases: Kubernetes logs and traces on S3
Small teams needing one observability tool
Front-end RUM and session replay with backend logs
